model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k), with the x-axis labeled "Number of completions (k)" and spanning from $2^0$ to $2^8$ on a logarithmic scale, marked at intervals of $2^0, 2^1, \ldots, 2^8$. The y-axis, labeled "Coverage," ranges from 0.4 to 0.9 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Four distinct models are compared: Llama-3B (blue circles, solid line), Llama-3B + FT (green triangles, solid line), Llama-1B (light blue diamonds, dashed line), and Llama-1B + FT (light green triangles, dashed line). All four lines show a generally increasing trend in coverage as the number of completions increases. At $2^0$, Llama-3B starts at approximately 0.45 and increases to 0.87 at $2^8$. Llama-3B + FT begins at 0.47 and reaches 0.88 at $2^8$. Llama-1B starts at 0.38 and rises to 0.85, while Llama-1B + FT starts at 0.4 and ends at 0.86. The lines for Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT are consistently above those for Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT, respectively, and all lines exhibit a smooth, upward curve, indicating improved coverage with more completions.
